data.one_liner: Generates Riverpod providers from annotated functions using build_runner.
data.what_it_does: It reads functions annotated with @riverpod and creates matching provider classes automatically. The generated providers support hot‑reload and full Riverpod features without manual boilerplate.
use_when: You want type‑safe Riverpod providers without writing boilerplate code
You need multiple parameters or named arguments for providers
You want stateful hot‑reload of providers during development
avoid_when: You cannot add a build step or prefer pure runtime definitions
Your project is tiny and the generator overhead isn’t justified
You need providers that must be defined dynamically at runtime
strengths: Supports multiple and named parameters for families
Enables stateful hot‑reload of individual providers
weaknesses: Adds a build_runner step and generated code to the project
Debugging generated code can be less straightforward
Only works for Dart/Flutter projects that can run code generation
data.setup_notes: Add riverpod_generator as a dev_dependency, ensure riverpod_annotation is in dependencies, run `dart run build_runner watch` or `build_runner build`. Optional build.yaml can customize provider name suffixes.

alternatives.name: riverpod
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides the same state‑management capabilities without code generation, suitable for simple or dynamic provider setups

alternatives.name: flutter_riverpod
alternatives.why_pick_it: Core Riverpod package for Flutter with manual provider definitions, no extra build step
